overview.title: Where the town meets the water
overview.p1: Al Hoceima’s port and corniche showcase the authentic, working side of the bay: colorful fishing boats, repair nets, fresh daily catches, and a lively promenade that comes alive as the evening air cools.
overview.p2: Rather than a historical medina, this is a vibrant, modern seafront. It offers picturesque bay viewpoints, lively cafés, and an authentic taste of local seaside life.
overview.p3: An ideal spot to start or wrap up your beach days. Most coastal boat excursions into the nearby national park coves depart directly from the harbour area.

q1.question: Is the port overly touristy?
q1.answer: No, it is primarily an active working fishing harbour, making it genuine, lively, and culturally interesting.

q2.question: Where is the best place to walk?
q2.answer: Stroll along the main corniche promenade toward the cliff lookouts, especially around sunset for the best views over the bay.

q3.question: Are there good fish restaurants nearby?
q3.answer: Yes, several fish restaurants and grill spots are located right around the port and nearby town streets, offering fresh daily catches.

q4.question: Is it safe to walk along the corniche at night?
q4.answer: Yes, the corniche is well-lit and popular with local families in the evenings; standard town precautions apply.

q5.question: How do I arrange boat trips from the port?
q5.answer: Short coastal trips and water taxis can be arranged directly with local skippers at the harbour — always confirm the price and duration before departing.
